svg.title: TOPAK C10 — A call's user scope is downstream: the mechanism binds the subject, the policy decides whether, the downstream system decides what, and the tool decides nothing
svg.desc: A Run tool that reads "the current user's documents" reaches a system that authorizes by user, and the corpus has no record of whose scope a call uses. The entry declares where a tool connects (ADR-0049 §5) and nothing about the credential it presents. ADR-0056 answers OWASP LLM06:2025's mitigation 5 and example 5. Carrying the user's scope in the lease would be wrong ⟨U1⟩. Leaving the binding to the model would be worse ⟨U2⟩. A subject travels with the grant, beside the lease, evidenced by its provider and fixed for the round. ADR-0056 is Proposed and nothing here is in force or built: no dependent entry is drafted, and no module, floor stage or reference addendum exists.
svg.text: TOPAK · C10

text.tspan: A call's user scope is downstream: the mechanism binds the subject, the policy decides whether, the downstream system decides what, and the tool decides nothing

svg.text: A Run tool that reads "the current user's documents" reaches a system that authorizes by user, and the corpus has no record of whose scope a call uses. The entry declares where a tool connects (ADR-0049 §5) and nothing about the credential it presents. ADR-0056 answers OWASP LLM06:2025's mitigation 5 and example 5. Carrying the user's scope in the lease would be wrong ⟨U1⟩. Leaving the binding to the model would be worse ⟨U2⟩. A

subject travels with the grant, beside the lease, evidenced by its provider and fixed for the round. ADR-0056 is Proposed and nothing here is in force or built: no dependent entry is drafted, and no module, floor stage or reference addendum exists.

Proposed means nothing here is in force. The custodian settled two things: a user's scope is enforced downstream and not carried in the lease ⟨U1⟩, and which user a call acts for is decided by the mechanism and the policy, not by the model ⟨U2⟩. The custodian asked whether the tool should decide. That the tool decides nothing is the drafter's answer (§1), and so is every other choice. C1 applies because a subject-bound credential is a new route by which an admitted call carries authority that

is not the deployment's own. C2 applies to §5: the tool host's premise widens. Every clause the mechanism applies subtracts, except binding a subject at grant, whose authority is the subject's provider's. One author, one day.

text.tspan: Today, a deployment has two choices, and both are bad

svg.text: One service identity that can reach every user's data. This is LLM06's example 5, a generic high-privileged identity standing in for the
user.
The tool picks a user's credential from something it was given, usually an input the Thinker wrote. This is the worse failure, and the
admit path cannot see it. An injected Thinker names another user, and the downstream system honours it. ADR-0047's F2 refuses a
literal destination after untrusted reads. A subject is not a destination, and nothing marks it.

text.tspan: Where the scope is enforced is not the problem ⟨U1⟩

svg.text: The membrane decides what crosses. What the downstream system does with a call it receives is its own authorization, as LLM06's
mitigation 7 asks.
A per-user credential can only make an admitted call do less. It weakens no theorem, and none needs to rest on it.
Not in the lease: every lease field is authority the mechanism grants and can check (ADR-0031 §1). A user's rights in a third-party
system are neither.

text.tspan: The problem is the binding: who decides which user ⟨U2⟩

svg.text: A wrong binding adds authority: another user's. By ADR-0045 §2's test, whatever decides it must be checked, or be a trust root with an
issued identity.
A model is neither, and a tool's behaviour is a claim (ADR-0049 §4). So the binding is a syntactic lift from something on the record
The corpus already has the shape: ADR-0050 §3 binds an operator to a provider's assertion naming the fence; ADR-0050 §5 carries
the task and its label with the grant, beside the lease.

text.tspan: Which user does this round act for?

svg.text: A syntactic lift from a provider-signed assertion carried with the grant (§2). Fixed for the round

text.tspan: May this call use that user's credential?

svg.text: The floor's minimum (§4), and the bundle may narrow on the subject's attributes. It never widens (ADR-0030)

text.tspan: What may the credential do downstream?

svg.text: Its own authorization, on the subject the credential names

text.tspan: Which credential does the tool present?

svg.text: Nobody: the tool host injects the one credential for the round's subject (§5)
The tool is handed exactly one credential and has no means to obtain another

text.tspan: A tool that chooses must hold every subject's credential

svg.text: That is the generic high-privileged identity of LLM06's example 5, moved from the network to the tool's memory.

text.tspan: A tool's behaviour is a claim

svg.text: The digest pins its code, not what it does with its inputs (ADR-0049 §2, §4). A choice made inside it is made past

text.tspan: A tool's choice is steered by its inputs

svg.text: Its inputs are the Thinker's. Letting the tool choose is letting the model choose, one step removed.
The tool decides nothing (drafter's choice; the custodian asked): three reasons

text.tspan: A round that acts for a user, end to end (§2, §4–§7)
B2 · The mechanism: grant and admit
The user: a subject, not a principal

svg.text: No seat, no lease, no alphabet, and never promoted (§2).
ADR-0037's one-seat-per-principal rule is untouched.
The party whose downstream authority a round's calls may
use.
Must be present at grant: a user who is not cannot be
acted for (finding 2).

text.tspan: Its key is on the issued rules' list of subject providers
A trust root for the subjects it vouches for, and for no

svg.text: others, as an operator's provider is (T-0045-35). One
provider may serve both.
Names the subject, the provider and the fence of the
grant it is presented for.

text.tspan: No wall clock is read: freshness is the fence.

svg.text: Its form is open: an OIDC ID token with a nonce bound to
the fence, or a token-exchange request (Open obligations).
A seating's quorum, or an operator's Regrant (ADR-0050

text.tspan: Cannot name a subject without that subject's

svg.text: assertion. So an operator cannot act as an arbitrary user,
and the subject is attributed to its provider's signature, not
to the operator's word.
The grant carries, beside the lease:
Closed field set, unchanged (ADR-0031 §1). No thirteenth field ⟨U1⟩.
Beside the lease (ADR-0050 §5; ADR-0031 A3).
Beside the lease, as the task is (§2; ADR-0031 A3, owed).
The assertion verifies under a listed provider key and names this grant's fence.
Otherwise the grant is refused.
The seating bounds it: whether its rounds may carry a subject, and from which providers. A
grant outside that bound is refused. A quorum decides that a seat acts for users. One
Fixed for the round: not added, changed or dropped inside it. Two users are two rounds.
Ends with the round: the lease's ttl bounds it (ADR-0031 A2). Nothing is refreshed inside
a round.
The lift adds to RunCtx, from the grant: subject.present, subject.provider,
subject.attributes; to the tool: credentialMode, subjectProviders. Mechanical and
total (ADR-0007).
R10 forbids a subject call in a round with no subject. R11 forbids one whose provider the
entry does not accept.
The bundle may narrow on subject.attributes. By bundle ⊑ floor it only denies
more: a provider's claim can subtract authority, and never add it.
No floor entry looks for a subject in the inputs. Telling whether free text names a user is
a judgment.
The grant record: the subject's provider and a digest of its identifier. An authority fact, so
it is in the forensic floor and survives erasure (ADR-0028).
The assertion's bytes are in the round's payload, inside the unit of erasure (ADR-0003).
Every Actuate on a subject entry is attributable to the subject through its round's grant.
The admit record gains no field.
An Observer and the correlator read the digest, as they read every grant fact.
Sees the tool list, which shows each entry's
credential.mode and scope, so it knows a call acts as its
user. It does not show the subject (ADR-0048 §2, owed).
Never sees the assertion or the credential: neither is
ingress, and the Listener never delivers them.
The task may name the user. That is content. So may
any input.
At each Actuate on a subject entry, obtains the credential for the
round's subject and presents it on the tool's one channel.
Exchange, not storage (drafter's choice): the round's assertion is
exchanged for a credential scoped to that subject, so no standing
per-user credential exists at rest.
For service, it injects the entry's service credential. For none, nothing.
Newly trusted to present only the round's subject's credential,
beside running only the allowlisted binary and binding its socket
Receives exactly one credential and no
means to obtain another.
Decides nothing. Its behaviour is a claim; the
digest pins its code (ADR-0049 §4).
A Thinker's input naming another user reaches
it as content.
Part of T-0045-39: excluded. No
theorem rests on it.

svg.text: as one (§6; ToO §13, owed). It
closes the free-text path that §4
leaves open.

①②③: the three closure points (Consequences; band 3)

text.tspan: The confused deputy is closed at three points, and each degeneracy reopens one (Consequences; §9)

svg.text: The mechanism (§2)
No subject without its assertion: signed under a listed key, naming this grant's fence, within the seating's
bound
D-0056-1 Declared subject: the subject is named by the operator's signed
grant, with no provider assertion
Attribution moves from the subject's provider to the operator. A havoc operator can act for any subject the seating admits. §2's bound still holds
The tool host (§5)
One credential per round: the round's subject's, obtained by exchange, and the tool has no means to obtain
another
D-0056-2 Stored credentials: the host selects a per-user credential from a store
rather than exchanging the round's assertion
The host's failure reaches every stored subject, not only the round's. The store becomes part of T-0045-25
The downstream system (§6)
It takes the subject from the credential, never from the request. An assumption of use, not a check
D-0056-3 Request-named subject downstream: the downstream system reads
the subject from the request
A Thinker's input names the user. The confused deputy is open, and only the bundle and the Observer stand against it

Deployment position: Archetype, with three degeneracies. Only ① is the mechanism's own check; ② rests on a trust root and ③ on an assumption of use. Finding 5: §6 carries the weight for free text, because the floor cannot find a user named in an input. The design moves that path to a system TOPAK does not verify, which is the position ⟨U1⟩, recorded as one.

text.tspan: The entry declares its credential, and the floor carries a minimum (§3, §4)

svg.text: §3: channel.credential, added to the channel part of a Run entry (ADR-0049 §1)
none · service · subject
Checked: the tool host injects by it (§5), and the floor reads it (§4)
For subject: the subject providers whose assertions this entry accepts
Checked: against the issued list at load (W12) and the round's subject at admit (R11)
Text: what the credential permits downstream
Claimed. What the downstream system enforces is its own
Load checks, added to ADR-0049 §6 after W1–W10. The bundle is refused when:
A Run entry's channel has no credential.mode, or a mode outside the three
A subject entry names no provider, or a provider the issued rules do not list, or has empty scope text
A none or service entry carries providers

The mode is required, with no default (drafter's choice), by the totality rule ADR-0047 §1 and ADR-0049 W4 apply. A Run entry without it does not load, so every Run entry changes form, and a bundle and policy change together.

service is permitted and is not the default: the deployment's own identity, right for a tool that reaches nothing per-user. Finding 3: service is where LLM06's example 5 survives. Whether a service entry reaches per-user data is a claim nothing checks;
scope and promotion are the only defence, as for purpose.
A Build entry has no channel, so it has no credential. ADR-0049 W5 already refuses one.
§4: two floor entries, ADR-0041's next free ids after the workflow stage's R8, R9
the tool's credentialMode is subject and subject.present is false
the tool's credentialMode is subject and subject.provider is not in the tool's subjectProviders
R11 duplicates what the tool host would fail anyway, and is kept so that the refusal is an admit decision on the record, not a failed call past the membrane (drafter's choice).
The bundle may narrow on subject.attributes, for example to allow an entry only for subjects in a named group. Such a rule can only deny more.
No floor entry looks for a subject in the inputs. That is a judgment, and ③ closes the path downstream instead.
Not taken: a floor forbid on service entries in a subject round. A service entry that reaches nothing per-user is legitimate, and the floor cannot tell which kind it is. The bundle may forbid it.

text.tspan: The floor stage that would carry them

svg.text: subjects, in floor/proposed/, built on the stage in force at ratification, with R10 and R11: validated, tested and gated, each entry shown to fire and none shown vacuous (§11). Not built.

text.tspan: The trusted base gains a root, a widened premise and an excluded row (§8)

svg.text: A subject provider
trust root
A round that acts for a subject who did not ask, within what the seating and floor allow
Issued (ADR-0025 §1 (f)), on the list of subject providers
A trust root for the subjects it vouches for, and no others
The tool host
trust root
As before, and a call presented with another subject's credential
Promotion: part of the release
Under D-0056-2 the credential store joins this row
A downstream system's authorization, and any token service that mints for
it
Whatever the credential permits, done for the subject it names
Nothing. No theorem rests on it ⟨U1⟩
The position, not a gap: a reader computing a deployment's guarantees sees that per-user scope is the downstream system's
T-0045-37 is the last row in force (ADR-0053, B36), so these are the next two ids. They join G1 at ratification. Every theorem stays about the membrane.

text.tspan: The subject in the lease, as a thirteenth field

svg.text: Rejected ⟨U1⟩. Every lease field is authority the mechanism grants (ADR-0031 §1). A subject's authority is its provider's, and it travels beside the lease as the task does

text.tspan: The subject as a Thinker input, checked by policy

svg.text: Rejected ⟨U2⟩. Whether the named user is the right one is a judgment about content (ADR-0007)
Rejected (§1). It needs every credential, its choice is a claim, and its inputs are the model's

text.tspan: A subject input marked as a

svg.text: Not taken. It stretches what a destination is, and it still lets a Thinker that has read only trusted content name any user
Rejected. A user is not promoted and holds no Persona, and a quorum per user does not scale. One entry or seating per tenant remains possible and is syntactic, so it needs no degeneracy
Not taken at the archetype. It is D-0056-1
Not taken (drafter's choice). It mixes two users' content in one round topic and one clearSet, and needs a per-call subject, which is a choice someone must make
Not taken. A service entry that reaches nothing per-user is legitimate, and the floor cannot tell which kind it is (finding 3). The bundle may forbid it

text.tspan: No record: leave per-user scope to deployments

svg.text: Rejected. The scope can be left to deployments, and §6 does. The binding cannot, because its failure adds authority

text.tspan: What is open, and what ratification needs (Findings; Open obligations; §10, §11)

svg.text: 1. The task path is the larger gap. Grants come from a quorum or an operator, and ADR-0050 §2's "the rate problem does not arise" assumed one operator acting
per round. A deployment serving users at volume reopens that rate problem.
2. Freshness by fence asks the user's session to be live at grant. The right failure direction, but it excludes scheduled or long-running work for a user.
3. service is where LLM06's example 5 survives (band 4).
4. Results from a subject call are that user's data, and nothing labels them so. A workflow edge (ADR-0054) could carry one user's data into another's round
unless the activation is per subject.
5. §6 is an assumption, and it carries the weight for free text (band 3).
How a user's request becomes a task. A round for a user today needs an operator to act. A separate record (finding 1).
Long-running or offline action for a user: refresh tokens, a scheduled job for an absent user.
Delegation between principals, which ADR-0054 decides by seating every cell.
A subject's consent, beyond its provider having signed an assertion naming the grant's fence.
The form of the subject assertion, and whether an existing token format carries it unchanged.
The size and form of subject.attributes, and which provider claims may be lifted.
A task path for end users: a record of its own.
Whether a digest of a personal identifier in the forensic floor meets a deployment's data obligations.
The label of a subject call's result: a per-subject sensitivity name in ADR-0047's vocabulary, or one the bundle declares.
ADR-0054's activation carrying one subject, if ADR-0054 is ratified first.
ADR-0050 confirmed first, or this record ratified provisionally with it.
The dependent entries drafted: ADR-0049 (§3's fields; W11–W13), ADR-0050 §5, ADR-0031 A3, ADR-0041 (R10, R11, the RunCtx attributes), ADR-0042 §6,
ADR-0045 (T-0045-38, T-0045-39, T-0045-25's premise), ADR-0025 A2, ADR-0048 §2, ToO §13, and ADR-0054 §2 if ratified first.
A module, by ADR-0046's method, whose mutations break its properties: SubjectFixedForRound, SubjectEvidenced, InjectedIsRoundSubject,
SubjectEntryNeedsSubject; M_INPUT_SUBJECT, M_RESUBJECT, M_STALE_ASSERTION, M_NO_R10.
The floor stage subjects (band 4).
The reference, with an ADR-0033 addendum: one subject entry over a stub downstream that authorizes by token. Each behaviour seen: a valid assertion binds;
one naming another fence is refused; a subject call in a subjectless round is refused by R10; a Thinker input naming another user is served for the token's
subject, not the input's; the tool list shows the mode and not the subject.
A reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2).
On-behalf-of attribution for an end user, which ADR-0037 lists as not owed, in one form: one subject per round, evidenced at grant. Delegation between principals
stays as ADR-0054 leaves it.
